summary: On-demand sampled SIEM playback suitable for subpoena with deterministic PII redaction rationale and legal attestation
description: Issue summary: Customer (VerityTel) requires an on-demand subset of audit events that is suitable for court/subpoena submission. They asked for a sampled playback that preserves event order fidelity, deterministic PII redaction (with rationale), and an auditable manifest and chain-of-custody statement signed by Redwood legal.
impact: Customer legal team cannot satisfy an active regulatory subpoena until they receive a forensically defensible export. This blocks their discovery timeline and may result in escalation to legal and account risk.
environment_details: Production tenant: veritytel-prod, ingestion via tenant-kafka-us-east, SIEM bridge configured to push ndjson to customer SFTP. Customer currently on enterprise contract and expects signed attestation artifacts.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Customer requests export via Console -> Support -> Evidence export (choose 'Forensic playback / Subpoena').

2) Support runs ad-hoc sampling tool with tenant id and time window: /internal/tools/forensic-export --tenant veritytel-prod --start 2026-02-14T00:00:00Z --end 2026-02-14T23:59:59Z --sample-rate 0.05 --seed 7421
3) Tool produces ndjson chunk files, manifest.json (including SHA256 checksums), and redaction log.csv with deterministic pseudonymization mapping seed and KMS-key fingerprint.
4) Customer verifies sample by downloading sample-playback.zip from pre-signed S3 link we provide and compares checksums in manifest.
Note: reproduction requires internal entitlement (support-forensics role) and HSM signing key access.

comments: 2026-03-05 - Support (Aisha): Initial request from VerityTel legal for a subpoena-ready subset; they explicitly asked for deterministic redaction rationale and a legal attestation. Asked for available timelines and what artifacts we can provide.

2026-03-05 - Customer (VerityTel legal): Required delivery window is 2026-03-08 for initial sample; final handoff may be required by 2026-03-12. Required artifacts: ndjson export, manifest with checksums, redaction rationale, and signed chain-of-custody PDF.

2026-03-06 - SRE (Liam): Confirmed we have tooling to produce deterministic sampled exports. Need HSM team to sign chain-of-custody. Proposed seed=7421 and sample-rate 5% to keep volume ~60k events for review.

2026-03-07 - Legal (Marina Ortiz): Drafted attestation template and asked for exact manifest fields to confirm legal language. Also requested reversible pseudonymization statement if applicable (customer prefers irreversible masking).

2026-03-08 - Support (Aisha): Delivered initial sample-playback.zip to customer, provided manifest and redaction rationale. Awaiting confirmation that redaction approach meets subpoena requirements. Customer asked for more detail on the deterministic mapping algorithm.
investigation_notes: Hypothesis 1: Customer needs deterministic redaction (HMAC with tenant-specific key) so that repeated exports map same identifiers consistently; this is supported by our RedactionEngine using tenant-KMS-derived key material.

Hypothesis 2: Legal requires non-reversible pseudonymization in the exported artifact; HSM signing of the manifest is sufficient for chain-of-custody but we must avoid storing reversible mappings in export.
Test run: Generated export with seed=7421 and sample-rate=0.05. Verified that repeated runs with same seed produced identical pseudonymized identifiers and identical manifest checksums.

Dashboard links: forensic-export job logs: https://internal-logs.redwood.company/forensic-export/7421 ; SIEM bridge delivery: https://grafana.redwood.company/d/siem/bridge-overview?orgId=1&from=1644816000000&to=1644902399000

Open items: 1) Confirm with HSM team ability to produce time-stamped signature for chain-of-custody PDF. 2) Confirm whether customer requires reversible mapping escrow (customer said they prefer irreversible). 3) Update public-runbook to include deterministic sampling parameters.
resolution: Workaround / Interim: Delivered a 5% deterministic sample (seed=7421) and manifest signed by forensics-signing key. Provided redaction rationale document that details deterministic-HMAC approach and non-reversible nature for exported artifacts.

Permanent Fix / Action Items: 1) HSM team to produce signed chain-of-custody PDF using key sign-prod-forensics (tracking PR: github.com/redwood-inference/audit-tools/pull/88). 2) Build console UI option 'Subpoena playback' that automates seed selection and manifest signing (owner: SIEM product). 3) Add a legal attestation checkbox and template for enterprise exports. 4) Document deterministic sampling in Confluence runbook (link added above).
Follow-up: Customer to confirm acceptance of non-reversible redaction. If customer requires reversible escrow, open a separate ticket to scope HSM escrow workflow and contractual implications.
Status: Initial sample delivered; awaiting 'Accepted' from VerityTel legal. If accepted, schedule HSM-signed chain-of-custody handoff by 2026-03-12.
notes_for_engineering: When re-running exports, ensure same seed and sample-rate are used to produce bit-for-bit identical pseudonymized fields. Add unit test covering deterministic mapping across versions of RedactionEngine.
Avoid including any mapping tables in exported artifacts; if reversible mapping is requested, require explicit contract and create separate escrow PR with approval from Legal and Security.
